title: Grill — Task card UI overhaul
summary:
The investigation found **why** the card in your screenshot breaks (all of it is settled under *What's already proven*). What's left are your calls: **14 questions** plus a short confirm-or-override list.

Start with the **Blocking** ones: scope, header layout, pipeline progress semantics and the action row. They decide the plan's shape. Everything else adjusts parts of it.

Fixed geometry to keep in mind: a card's content box is **225 px wide** in every window size (`w-72` column). Source brief: `docs/plans/task-card-ui-overhaul-investigation.md`.

proven.text: **Header overflow root cause.** `TaskCard` passes `shrink-0` to `PipelineBadge` (and to the profile badge and `StackBadge`), cancelling the badge's own `min-w-0 truncate`. In the 225 px row, `justify-between` falls back to `flex-start`: the left cluster collapses to 0 px, the pill covers the type icon by 6 px, and the stack chip lands 27 px past the card's edge. Reproduced exactly in Chromium with the repo's Tailwind config.

evidence.label: the badge is built to truncate
evidence.code: className={cn("inline-flex min-w-0 max-w-full items-center gap-1.5 border-transparent font-normal", STATUS_CLASSES[run.status], className)} > {run.pipelineName}

proven.text: **`13/10` is a counting bug.** `pipelineStepProgress` counts *executions*, not steps. Your screenshot task ran Code Review 3× and Bug Fix 2× on a 10-step graph → 13 succeeded executions. 107 of 120 done pipeline runs in your prod DB over-count (max: 79 on a 9-step graph).

proven: **Gate-pending action row overflows by 48 px** (Open + Review + Stop + Diff + Delete; Delete sits 31 px outside the card). The `Answer (N) →` row fits with 0 px spare, so `Answer (12)` overflows.
**The dark-mode `Done` hole** is `variant="outline"` painting `bg-background`, which is darker than `--card` in dark mode only.
**Raw markdown preview:** 355 of 399 active tasks have markdown-looking prompts (`# Spec…`, tables, fences).

**No server, DB, route or migration change is needed** for any option below. The progress fix is one pure function in `src/shared/`, which also fixes the run view, `agetor ls/show/pipeline` and the TUI (they show the same wrong number today).
**The existing tests would not catch any of this:** the header e2e seeds only a plain harness badge, and no progress test repeats a step.

questions.title: How far does this change go?
questions.why: Fix-only is ~5 targeted edits; the redesign touches the header, action row, preview, chips and accessibility, and re-baselines ~20 e2e specs that locate the card.
questions.context: Your goal said *"improve the Card UI following the best UI/UX practices"*, not just *"fix the overflow"*. Questions 3–14 below only matter in full (or partial) form; if you pick **Fix only**, answer them anyway where you have a view — they'll be recorded as out of scope.

options.label: Full redesign
options.description: Fix every breakage **and** rework the card: header layout, action row with overflow menu, plain-text preview, title clamp, one chip system, consistent button sizes, focus/keyboard, density.
options.consequence: Bigger plan; every card state gets a geometry e2e check; supersedes the 2026-09-01 header decision where you say so below.

options.label: Fix the breakage only
options.description: Header overflow, `13/10`, gate-pending overflow, dark `Done` hole, the amber literal.
options.consequence: Small and safe; the raw-markdown preview, 5 chip styles, button height mismatch and a11y gaps stay.

options.label: Fix + the items I tick below
options.description: Fix the breakage, and take only the redesign items you pick in the later questions.
options.consequence: Plan scope is whatever the later answers add.

recommendation.reason: Your goal asks for best-practice UI, and most of the 'not broken' findings (raw markdown, 4 px button mismatch, no focus ring) are visible on every card.

questions.title: Do you want to see a visual mockup before code is written?
questions.why: Adds a sign-off gate between planning and coding.

options.label: Yes: Planning publishes an HTML mockup of the chosen layout
options.description: Every card state (idle, running, awaiting, gate-pending, review, done, archived, pipeline + stack + long names), light and dark, at the real 262 px width.
options.consequence: One extra round with you before coding; layout surprises get caught there instead of in review.

options.label: Yes, with 2–3 layout alternatives to pick from
options.consequence: Your header/action answers below become a starting point, not final.

options.label: No, go straight from these answers to the plan
options.consequence: First visual check is the running dev build.

recommendation.reason: It's a visual change; one mockup of the layout you choose here is cheap and catches what words miss, without reopening every decision.

sections.title: Header & pipeline pill
sections.intro: Today: row 1 = type icon + count badges … identity chip (pipeline / profile / harness) + stack chip; row 2 = right-aligned `model · mode` alone; row 3 = title, unclamped. That shape was your decision on 2026-09-01 (`docs/plans/task-card-header-rows.md`, PR #206); the pipeline pill (#244) and stack chip (#295) arrived later and broke it.

questions.title: Pipeline cards: where do the pipeline name, progress and active step go?
questions.why: The pill today reads `⧉ <pipeline name> 3/10 · <active step>` in one line; in 225 px something must give.
questions.context: Real names in your DB: pipelines up to 26 chars (`My Implementation Pipeline`), step names like `Implementing`, `Code Review`. A stack chip (`1/2`) may share the row.

options.label: Pill keeps name + progress (name truncates, progress never does); active step gets its own line under the title
options.consequence: The step you'd glance for is never truncated; one extra line while a step is active or a gate is pending.
options.preview:
│ ▣          ⧉ Zebra Pipel… 3/10  1/2│
│ Acme Sync - Keep the inbox…     │
│ ▶ Implementing                  │

options.label: One pill; the pipeline name truncates first, step name kept
One pill; the step name truncates first, pipeline name kept

recommendation.reason: The active step is the live status (what is it doing now?); squeezing two variable-length names into one pill guarantees one of them is unreadable.

questions.title: Should long titles be clamped?
questions.why: Reopens the 2026-09-01 'no title clamp' decision. Titles reach 128 chars in your DB (≈5 lines at 225 px; average is 33).

options.label: Clamp to 3 lines, full title in the tooltip and the run panel
options.consequence: Cards stay a predictable height; the rare long title is cut.

options.label: Clamp to 2 lines
Keep full wrap (the 2026-09-01 decision)
options.consequence: Long titles still make 5-line cards.

recommendation.reason: 3 lines covers ~95-char titles in full, so only the outliers are cut, and the board stays scannable.

sections.title: Pipeline progress semantics
sections.intro: This changes the number everywhere: board pill, run-view header, `agetor ls`, `agetor show`, `agetor pipeline` and the TUI dashboard, all through `pipelineStepProgress`.

questions.title: What should `n/total` mean for a pipeline with loops and branches?
questions.why: Picks the counting rule and its unit tests; every surface changes at once.
questions.context: Counting **distinct** completed steps fixes `13/10` → `10/10`, but **15 of your 120 done runs** would read `9/10`, because a branch was never taken (review passed the first time, so Bug Fix never ran).

options.label: Distinct completed steps / total; a finished run reads `✓ Done`
options.description: Running: `3/10`. Done: `✓ Done` (the skipped branch can't make a finished run look unfinished). Failed / cancelled: distinct `n/total` in the status colour, as today.
options.consequence: Never exceeds the total; finished runs never look short.

options.label: Distinct completed steps / total, always
options.consequence: Done runs with an untaken branch read `9/10`.

options.label: Position along the path actually taken
options.description: Only steps on the taken path count toward the total.
options.consequence: Total can change mid-run as branches resolve; harder to explain and test.

recommendation.reason: Fixes both the over-count and the misleading 9/10, with a simple rule that's easy to unit-test.

questions.title: Where should the execution/loop count (e.g. "13 step runs · 2 loops") still appear?
questions.why: The executions are real information (how many review cycles it took); the fix removes them from the headline number.

options.label: Board pill tooltip
Pipeline run-view header
`agetor show` / `agetor pipeline` output
Nowhere; drop it

recommendation.reason: Loop count is how you see a review/bug-fix cycle went long; keep it one hover or one command away, off the headline.

sections.title: Action row
sections.intro: The row is `flex gap-1`, no wrap, no overflow handling. Icon buttons are `h-9`, text buttons `h-8`. The right-click menu (`buildTaskContextMenu`) already offers Open/Review/Run/Stop/Mark done/Archive, View changes, Open in Finder, PR/issue links, copy branch/path and Delete…, and mirrors the card's button precedence.

questions.title: How should the action row fit in 225 px?
questions.why: Decides the button set per state, whether a `⋯` menu exists, and which e2e selectors move (`getByTitle("View changes (git diff)")` in 2 specs; `button[title="Stop"]` count in 1).
questions.context: An earlier grill (pipeline human gate) decided: **Review primary, Open visible, Stop a visually secondary danger action.** Options below keep that unless noted.

options.label: Primary (+ one secondary) + Diff icon + `⋯` menu
options.description: State's primary button, plus `Done`/`Open` where relevant; Diff stays one click; `⋯` opens the existing context menu at the button with Archive, Stop-extra and Delete… inside. Gate-pending: Review · Open · Stop (icon, danger) · ⋯.
options.consequence: Always fits; Delete and Archive become two clicks; one menu to maintain (already exists).

options.label: Primary only + `⋯` menu (Diff goes in the menu too)
options.consequence: Cleanest row; Diff becomes two clicks.

options.label: Keep every icon visible, compact (`h-7`), allow wrapping to a 2nd line
options.consequence: Nothing hidden; some states get a 2-line action row.

options.label: Reveal secondary icons on hover / keyboard focus
options.consequence: Clean at rest; actions invisible until hover — poor discoverability, no hover on the mobile companion.

recommendation.reason: Diff is the most-used secondary action; Delete/Archive are rare and destructive, so one extra click is a feature. Reusing the context menu keeps the precedence mirror in one place.

questions.title: What should the 2-line prompt preview show?
questions.why: Decides whether a markdown-to-text helper is written (none exists) and what it extracts.
questions.context: Your screenshot card shows `# Spec — Keep the inbox watched for the whole session | Field | Value | | --- |…`. Plain stripping would give `Spec — Keep the inbox watched… Field Value …`, which repeats the title. Persisted prompts stay raw either way (rendering-only, client-side).

options.label: First prose paragraph as plain text
options.description: Skip headings, tables, rules, code fences and front-matter-like blocks; strip emphasis/link syntax; if no prose remains, fall back to stripped text; empty → no preview line.
options.consequence: New pure helper + unit tests; the preview shows the actual request.

options.label: Strip markdown syntax only, keep everything in order
options.consequence: Simpler helper; spec-style prompts still preview as `Spec — … Field Value …`.

options.label: First-prose plain text, and hide the preview on pipeline parents
options.consequence: Pipeline cards are shorter; their spec isn't previewed at all.

options.label: Remove the preview entirely

recommendation.reason: The preview's job is 'what was asked'; headings and tables are structure, not content.

sections.title: Accessibility & keyboard
sections.intro: Today the card root gets dnd-kit's `role="button"` + `tabIndex=0` while containing real buttons (axe `nested-interactive`), has no `focus-visible` style, and Enter/Space does nothing (only `PointerSensor`, `distance: 6`).

questions.title: Which accessibility items are in this change?
questions.why: Each is a separate piece of work and test; keyboard dragging is the large one.

options.label: Visible `focus-visible` ring on the card (semantic `ring` token)
Enter / Space on a focused card opens it (same as click)
Fix the button-inside-a-button: card keeps whole-surface pointer drag, but its role becomes a labelled group instead of `button`
options.description: Alternative (drag handle via `setActivatorNodeRef`) would change what's draggable — only the handle — so not offered as default.

options.label: `aria-label` on every icon-only button
Keyboard dragging between columns (`KeyboardSensor`)
options.description: Move a focused card with Space + arrows. A board feature more than a card one; touches App.tsx's DnD setup and drop handling.

recommendation.reason: The first four are card-local and cheap; keyboard dragging is a board-level feature that deserves its own ticket.

questions.title: If keyboard dragging is not in this change: out of scope, or deferred by you?
questions.why: Every remainder needs a disposition; nothing gets silently dropped.
questions.context: If you **did** tick keyboard dragging above, pick *It's in* here.

options.label: Owner-deferred: a later ticket
Out of scope: not wanted
It's in (I ticked it above)

recommendation.reason: Worth doing, but it's a board feature with its own drop/precedence rules.

questions.title: Which density/consistency changes are in?
questions.why: Each changes measured geometry the e2e checks will pin.
questions.context: Today: five chip styles (pipeline pill `text-xs rounded-full filled`, agent badge `text-xs font-semibold`, count badges `text-[10px] outline`, stack chip `text-[10px] rounded` 4 px, drifted chip `rounded filled`); buttons `h-8` vs icon `h-9`; card padding `p-4`; workdir and branch on two 10 px mono lines.

options.label: One chip system: one height (`h-5`), `text-[10px]`, `rounded-full`, same padding; colour carries the meaning
One button height on the card (`h-7` text and icon buttons)
Card padding `p-4` → `p-3` (content 225 → 233 px)
Workdir + branch on one line: repo folder name · branch (full path and branch in the tooltip)

recommendation.reason: Each removes a visible inconsistency or a wasted line; all are card-local (the shared Badge/Button primitives stay untouched).

questions.title: What has to pass before this is done?
questions.why: Today nothing would catch a regression of the screenshot.

options.label: e2e: every child of the card stays inside the card's box, for each state (pipeline + profile + stack + long names; gate-pending; awaiting `Answer (12)`; all count badges)
Unit: progress with a loop history (repeated stepIds), an untaken branch, and done/failed/cancelled runs; CLI `ls`/`show` tests updated
Unit: markdown-to-preview helper (headings, tables, fences, emphasis, links, empty)
Screenshots of the card states in light and dark, attached to the PR
You eyeball it in `bun run dev:hmr` before merge

recommendation.reason: The bounds check is the regression test for your screenshot; the theme screenshots catch the dark-only class of bug (`Done` today).

questions.title: Anything else that must be true before you'd call this done?
questions.placeholder: e.g. the companion app's card should match

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Defaults I'd bet on. One click each, or write what it should be.

questions.title: Answer button colour

recommendation.value: Replace `bg-amber-500 text-amber-950 …` with `bg-warning-solid` plus a new `--warning-solid-foreground` token (dark amber text, added to both `index.css` themes and `tailwind.config.js`). Card-local; the shared awaiting ring/glow and `StepNode` look stay unchanged.
recommendation.reason: Repo rule: semantic tokens only. `--warning-solid` exists in both themes, but it has no foreground pair yet.

questions.title: Done button in dark mode

recommendation.value: Card-local `bg-transparent` on the outline `Done` (no change to the shared Button variant).
recommendation.reason: Fixes the dark-only hole without touching every other outline button in the app.

questions.title: No `overflow-hidden` on the card

recommendation.value: Fix the flex layout instead of clipping; the card stays `overflow-visible`.
recommendation.reason: Clipping would hide the unread dot and awaiting glow, and would hide future overflow bugs instead of exposing them.

questions.title: Column width

recommendation.value: Columns stay `w-72`; resizable/wider columns are a different ticket.
recommendation.reason: A wider column would hide the overflow without fixing it.

questions.title: Shared UI primitives

recommendation.value: `ui/badge`, `ui/button`, `ui/card` variants are not changed; the card uses card-local classes (or a new, card-only chip component).
recommendation.reason: They're used app-wide.

questions.title: Where the preview helper lives

recommendation.value: `src/mainview/lib/prompt-preview.ts` + sibling test (webview only; the CLI/TUI don't show prompt previews).
recommendation.reason: No second consumer today; moving it to `src/shared/` later is a cheap move.

questions.title: Docs

recommendation.value: Update `task-context-menu.md` (card ↔ menu precedence, `⋯` entry), `pipelines.md` (progress rule), `PipelineBadge` doc comment, the header e2e spec comment; add a 'superseded by' note to `docs/plans/task-card-header-rows.md`.
recommendation.reason: Each describes behaviour this change alters.

questions.title: Companion (mobile) app card

recommendation.value: Out of scope: this change is the desktop webview card only.
recommendation.reason: Separate codebase and layout; only the shared progress rule reaches it if it uses `pipelineStepProgress`.
